transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Luis Ortega (Redwood) — Anika Rao, Tom Hargreaves, Priya Singh, Jayden (Crestline)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick consensus on pilot scope: 2-week sandbox with INT8 & FP8 profiles, run bench on 2k prompts, decision threshold for quality drop at >3% on Rouge-L / domain metric.

[00:00:05] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i think we said 45 minutes, we'll try to stick to it. maya from redwood, with luis our systems se. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Anika: good, thanks. excited to see the precision playbook. we've been tracking the int8 stuff but worried about edge-case hallucinations.
[00:00:22] Luis: yeah, totally. we'll start with the high-level tradeoffs then jump into the console — show you the optimize presets and a little sandbox benchmark. apologies if the demo is a bit choppy, connection may lag.
[00:00:37] Tom: quick ask — is this the hosted sandbox or VPC? we need to keep traces in our VPC for compliance.
[00:00:44] Maya: good call — for this pilot we'll provision a VPC-peered sandbox. you'll get a private endpoint and credentials. priya, we'll also need your CIDR for the peering.
[00:00:55] Priya: noted, i'll send it after the call.

[00:01:20] Luis: ok slide-free demo to save time — starting Optimize console. top of the page you can pick a model variant, then precision profiles. we have two curated presets for this flow: "Low-latency INT8" and "Balanced FP8". note: the names are suggestive, you can tune bucket thresholds.
[00:01:36] Anika: what are the default thresholds?
[00:01:39] Luis: default fidelity guard is a 2.5% degradation on your chosen eval metric — can be Rouge-L or a custom SLO. latency SLO is configurable per route. the UI warns when expected degradation exceeds threshold. sometimes the UI reads as "Reed wood Optima" in transcripts — ignore that :)
[00:01:57] Jayden: ha, lol.

[00:02:20] Luis: live: i'll create a gated rollout: 10% traffic to INT8, monitor eval on sampled outputs and latency p50/p95. if quality drops beyond threshold, rollback to FP8 automatically. the rollout policy also supports canary windows or step increments.
[00:02:40] Tom: does the rollback keep the KV cache warm when rolling back? that was a pain with our previous provider.
[00:02:48] Luis: good question — yes, we have a hybrid fallback that keeps hot KV segments warmed. when a fast variant rolls back to a slightly slower variant we avoid cold-start artifacts by continuing to maintain a shared cache layer for pinned prefixes. that reduces spike latency on fallback.

[00:03:15] Anika: and for worst-case fidelity — how do you measure? we use domain-specific scoring not just bleu/rouge.
[00:03:22] Luis: you can upload your eval harness. in the sandbox we'll preconfigure your provided metrics. the Optimize console lets you map any custom scorer to the fidelity guard. it will surface per-prompt deltas and so-called "shock points" where degradation concentrates.

[00:03:58] Maya: interrupting — quick commercial note: hosted pricing unit is per-token, dedicated can get you better throughput. for this pilot we'll keep you on our private sandbox, no charge for the trial aside from usage.
[00:04:10] Priya: good. we need audit logs and KMS integration for storing keys.
[00:04:14] Maya: we will enable KMS and generate audit hooks. i'll include SOC2 summary in the notes.

[00:04:40] Luis: back to demo — show the benchmark runner. i'm uploading a 250-sample set (demo set) — the console runs INT8 then FP8 and reports p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and a per-sample fidelity delta.
[00:04:55] (silence, some keyboard noises)
[00:05:18] Luis: results: INT8 gives ~28% token/sec improvement, p95 latency down from 420ms to 300ms on this small sample; however, we see a handful of outliers where the semantic score drops 4-6% on those prompts. that is exactly why we recommend a gated rollout.
[00:05:38] Tom: what's the distribution of deg? is it concentrated on long-context prompts?
[00:05:42] Luis: mostly yes — long-context and examples with rare named entities. INT8 quantization tends to clip some subtle attention weights. for those, FP8 preserves fidelity.

[00:06:10] Maya: quick Q for Tom — what's your latency SLO at p95? and what's the acceptable quality delta?
[00:06:17] Tom: p95 target is 350ms for interactive UI. quality delta we'd like <= 3% on our internal metric — beyond that we risk user-perceived regressions.
[00:06:26] Maya: ok that's in-line with default Optimize guard — we'll set the fidelity guard to 3% for the pilot.

[00:06:45] Luis: showing the precision playbook: stage 1: sample-based evaluation (sanity run); stage 2: canary (10-20% traffic); stage 3: progressive step-up to 100% with monitoring and scheduled verification. at each stage the system runs a telemetry sweep and flags regressions.
[00:07:03] Anika: how do you handle model drift or prompt distribution changes?
[00:07:07] Luis: the policy supports periodic re-evaluation window and rolling sampling that re-scores a sliding window of incoming traffic. if drift is detected the system can auto-trigger a re-run of the qprofile sweep or revert to a safer profile.

[00:07:35] Jayden: can we set different rules per route? our support chat vs summarization route have different tolerances.
[00:07:40] Maya: yes, per-route configs are supported in the console. you'll be able to pin different fidelity budgets.

[00:08:05] Priya: network question — during the pilot, will embeddings or logs leave our VPC?
[00:08:10] Luis: no; the VPC-peered sandbox keeps tokens and logs in your managed network. metrics are forwarded to our control plane metadata only — we can redact payloads. KMS can keep keys in your account.

[00:08:35] Tom: could we see the raw diffs for the dropped prompts?
[00:08:38] Luis: yes — the diff viewer surfaces token-level highlights and the scorer delta, with side-by-side outputs. note the transcriber here sometimes spells Redwood as "Read-wood" in the transcript export.

[00:09:05] (demo continues, screen share)
[00:09:28] Luis: now the decision matrix — here's a heatmap that maps percent latency improvement vs percent fidelity loss. we add color bands for acceptable regions. your product team can pick which region to operate in.
[00:09:45] Anika: that heatmap is helpful. any advice for fallback rules? immediate fallback vs queued rollback?
[00:09:52] Luis: immediate fallback for safety-critical routes; queued rollback for user-visible where you can take a small window to evaluate. fallback options: route-level pin to FP8, divert to dedicated capacity, or lower sequence-length cap to reduce exposure.

[00:10:20] Tom: what about KV cache consistency across variants — is that eventual or strong?
[00:10:24] Luis: we do eventual consistency for KV metadata but use a pinned prefix strategy to guarantee hot-path strong semantics for critical prefixes. there's a small tradeoff with memory, but it's configurable.

[00:11:00] Maya: let's walk through a sample runbook for rollback: trigger -> alert -> annotated diffs -> snapshot comparison -> automatic fallback to pinned FP8 -> ticket creation in your Jira. we can wire that to your webhook.
[00:11:19] Anika: good, we need the webhook and Jira mapping.
[00:11:24] Maya: will include in the notes and the action items.

[00:11:50] Luis: performance caveat — on shorter prompts INT8 rarely hurts fidelity and gives solid latency wins; on long-context doc-summarization you should be careful and prefer balanced FP8 or hybrid per-layer mixed-precision if available.
[00:12:10] Tom: hybrid per-layer options — do you expose layer-wise quantization?
[00:12:15] Luis: not in the console by default, it's an advanced qprofile we can enable for you in the sandbox. it allows preserving higher precision on specific attention layers. that tends to reduce those rare semantic regressions but is more complex to manage.

[00:12:40] Jayden: timeline question — our Q1 launch is mid-March. can the two-week pilot fit into our release cadence?
[00:12:47] Maya: yes, if we start the sandbox first week of Feb we can finish evaluation by end of Feb and have a rollout plan in March.

[00:13:10] (15-minute deeper technical pause where Luis runs automated bench; soft typing sounds)
[00:28:35] Luis: sharing consolidated bench: INT8 median latency 230ms, FP8 median 320ms on our selected instance. p95 difference narrows when we enable KV pre-warm. fidelity drops concentrated on ~1.2% of prompts.
[00:28:55] Tom: 1.2% concentrated — can we get the list and see their classes?
[00:29:00] Luis: yes, per-sample tags included. most are rare named entities, some are long arithmetic chains.

[00:29:30] Priya: infra-wise, we'd want to limit instance types. which GPUs are these?
[00:29:34] Luis: this run used A100s in FP8 mode and Hopper-like chips for the INT8 path analogy — sorry, the transcript sometimes mangles hardware names. we'll include exact SKUs in the workbook.

[00:30:05] Anika: security again — can you provide SOC2 and ISO docs and an overview of retention for logs in the sandbox?
[00:30:11] Maya: yes — i'll attach SOC2 attestation, ISO summary, and the sandbox retention policy (default 30 days but configurable).

[00:30:40] Tom: on the bench sheet, can we add our custom metric which is the last-mile extraction F1?
[00:30:45] Luis: absolutely — bring us the evaluation script and we'll plug it into the bench harness; results will be visible in the dashboard.

[00:31:10] Jayden: question on pricing exposure — worst-case cost if we run INT8 profiles across all traffic?
[00:31:16] Maya: INT8 reduces per-token inference cost but might increase calibration/ops cost. we'll run the cost projection in the workbook for your traffic profile and show the delta across scenarios.

[00:31:42] Tom: any known failure modes for INT8 to be aware of?
[00:31:45] Luis: the main ones: rare token degradation on low-frequency entities, increased instability on long generation chains, and quantization noise when sequence-length changes dramatically. we map those in the "shock point" reports.

[00:32:10] Anika: end-game question — if we decide to go hybrid (some routes INT8, others FP8), does Redwood manage the routing and billing split?
[00:32:17] Maya: yes, routing is policy-driven and billing is broken down by route and variant. you'll see token-level cost allocation in the console.

[00:32:40] (wrap-up)
[00:32:45] Maya: recap: we agreed on a 2-week VPC-peered sandbox, add 2k prompt set from tom, set fidelity guard to 3%, start canary at 10%. maya will provision sandbox and send bench workbook; luis will prepare stress script; priya to send CIDR.
[00:33:05] Anika: sounds good. can we do a hands-on infra session for priya and her team?
[00:33:09] Luis: yes, i'll set a 2-hour slot for the infra onboarding.

[00:33:30] Tom: last quick one — do you support audit snapshots for every rollout event? we need an immutable record.
[00:33:35] Maya: yes, the platform stores immutable rollout events and diffs, and we can push them into your S3 or your log sink.

[00:33:50] (minute of chit-chat)
[00:34:20] Maya: thanks everyone for your time. i'll follow up with the action items and the links.
[00:34:26] Anika: thanks, appreciate it.

[00:34:35] End meeting.
